Idea: Balance body at rest, then test
Low replication, idea persisted

title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging: Basics
text:
What is MRI?



Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Imaging:

Certain nuclei (H+) align with magnetic field
Respond to secondary field
Emit electromagnetic signal

Number of discoveries:

Rabi - NMR (molecular beams)
Bloch and Purcell - NMR (liquids, solids)
Lauterbur and Mansfield - MRI

Intersection: Physics, Engineering, CompSci, Neuroscience, Psychology









Isidor Rabi (1938) first described NMR; Nobel Prize 1944
Felix Bloch, Edward Purcell extended to liquids, solids; Nobel Prize 1952
Lauterbur, Mansfield; biologically useful MRI, EPI; Nobel Prize 2003

Safety Considerations



Rarely are rooms fatal
Strict Zoning helps
Diligence: avoid complacency and survivorship bias
Magnetic field has significant acceleration
Injuries are more common than they should be









Survivor bias: seatbelts, climbing (Rope on chair)

title: T1-Weighted Signal
text:
MRI data types


Ability to gather different types of data

Term: MRI sequence
Callibrated for distinct tissue properties

Examples:

T1w: gray vs white matter
T2w: fat vs water
Flair: white matter lesions
DWI: diffusion of water molecules
SWI: compounds that distort magnetic field

title: T1-Weighted Signal
text:
Protocols and contrast
Calibrated protocol for tissue differences Contrast - Protons - Diffusion - Hb, dOHb Underlay - dynamics in field

title: T1-Weighted Signal
text:
Precession



Protons - slightly positive (H+)
Inherent spin

Precession
Magnetic moment

Align with magnetic field

Low, high energy states
Net Magnetization
Frequency (Larmor)

Critical:

Known proton properties
Control protons with field gradients

title: T1-Weighted Signal
text:
Excitation



Engage with protons

Provide resonant electromagnetic radiation
Same frequency as known precession (Larmor)
Radiofrequency Pulse (42.58 MHz/T)

Protons flip from low to high energy state
Energy lost as thermal over time

T1 recovery
Differing rates

Not sufficient for imaging

Collect data only in transverse plain
